# duckduckgo-search-cli

> Chrome-only Rust CLI that turns a DuckDuckGo query into a JSON envelope an agent can route: declared discriminators, published JSON Schemas, and agent-native reduction operators that either act or refuse by name.

Every run is one process — spawn, search, reap, exit — with no daemon, no remote telemetry, and no product environment variables: configuration is CLI flags over XDG `config.toml` over compiled defaults. Reach for `llms.txt` when you need the compact agent contract, `llms-full.txt` when you need the extended history and the embedded documentation dump, and `duckduckgo-search-cli commands` when you need the live capability matrix instead of a table that can go stale.

- Rust CLI for DuckDuckGo search — returns results as JSON, Markdown, or plain text
- Install with: `cargo install duckduckgo-search-cli --locked`
- Current version: **v1.0.6**
- Repository: https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/duckduckgo-search-cli
- Production transport: **Chrome-only** chromiumoxide/CDP (GAP-WS-113). Without Chrome → exit 2 fail-closed.
- No remote telemetry. Product config = **CLI + XDG only** (no product env knobs).


## What's new in v1.0.6 (2026-08-21) — make the registry match the tree
- The version crates.io served did **not** compile on macOS or Windows; 1.0.6 is the installable line again
- Root cause closed: no gate linked "fixed in the tree" to "served by the registry", and `verify_published` now does
- `cargo yank` of 1.0.2 and 1.0.1 happens **after** publishing 1.0.6, because `max_stable_version` is derived from yank state
- The distributed profile now compiles with `--all-targets`; it previously failed with 91 errors, three of them the same `E0432` class as the shipped defect
- `completions bash | head -1` exits **141** instead of panicking
- `config set A B --key C` now **fails closed** with a usage exit; it used to write `C = B` and discard `A` in silence
- NEVER mix the positional form with the `--key` / `--value` form on `config get`, `config set` or `config unset`
- `--no-input` is now actually read at both stdin entry points; it used to be declared and never consumed
- SERP truncation now cuts on a UTF-8 boundary; an accented pt-BR page used to panic
- The WebRTC mitigation was inverted and re-exposed the local IP; it is corrected, and `--disable-features` no longer collides with itself
- `h2` moved to **0.4.18**, closing RUSTSEC-2026-0258 on the path that reaches the shipped binary
- ADR: `docs/decisions/0032-post-publish-verification-gate-v1-0-6.md`


## What's new in v1.0.5 (2026-08-10) — close the class by ruler, not by list

- **`--probe` / `--probe-deep` now honour the operators.** They emitted through `emit_probe_payload`, which never reached the projector, so on v1.0.4 `--count-only`, `--limit 1`, `--fields status` and `--truncate-content 5` each returned **633 bytes against a 633-byte baseline, at exit 0**. `emit_probe` now RETURNS the exit code, so a refusal reaches the caller instead of being swallowed by `let _ =`.
- **Identity strings are exempt from `--truncate-content`.** `schema --truncate-content 12` turned `invoke` into `duckduckgo-s` and `id` into `searc`. The rule: **a string the agent hands back to a program is IDENTITY, not content** — config keys, locale tags, schema ids, filesystem paths, probe error codes — declared per surface in `EnvelopeShape::identity` and published through `commands`.
- **Identity-only surfaces REFUSE `--truncate-content` with exit 2.** On `config list`, `config path`, `config get/set/unset`, `config effective` and `locale` every string is an identifier, so truncation returned 1138 bytes against a 1138-byte baseline — the signature of the original defect.
- **Refusal has ONE contract.** `output::emit_envelope_or_refuse` serves every surface including the probe: stdout carries `{"error", "message"}` (the published `error-response` shape, so a refusal is as routable as the success it replaces), stderr carries the localized sentence, exit stays **2**. The stdout `message` stays English on purpose — it is the machine half of the contract.
- **`agent_ops[].discriminator` → `agent_ops[].discriminator_key`.** The field published the VALUE (`doctor`, `schema_catalog`) while every envelope carries the KEY `type`. Agents trusting the matrix went looking for a key named `doctor`.
- **Four new XDG probe-timeout keys:** `probe_launch_timeout_seconds`, `probe_extract_timeout_seconds`, `probe_deep_launch_timeout_seconds`, `probe_deep_extract_timeout_seconds` — CLI, then XDG, then compiled default. A shorter `--timeout` still wins.
- **Refusal sentences are localized** (`Message` variants in `en` / `pt_br`); `--fields` now applies to a **timed-out** search too.
- Rulers, not lists: `tests/integration_stdout_boundary.rs` (every stdout emission outside `src/output/` must declare a reason) and `tests/integration_agent_ops_matrix.rs` (every operator × every offline surface must either drop bytes or exit 2).


## What's new in v1.0.4 (2026-08-09) — nothing accepted and ignored

- **The seven agent-native operators act or refuse BY NAME. There is no third outcome.** `--fields`, `--filter`, `--limit`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--count-only` and `--truncate-content` were declared on the root argument set but implemented per concrete type, so every other surface accepted them, exited `0`, and emitted a byte-for-byte unchanged envelope (`doctor --fields type`: 2523 bytes against a 2524-byte baseline).
- `--fields` and `--truncate-content` have meaning on any JSON object and apply everywhere. The five row operations need an array of rows; a **rowless** surface refuses them with exit `2`, naming the flag, the surface, and what IS supported there.
- **The row array is DECLARED per surface, never inferred** — `doctor` carries both `checks` and `failed_checks`; `config effective` carries both `allowed_keys` and `precedence`.
- **Measured:** `commands` 6421 → 47 bytes with `--fields version`; `doctor` 2524 → 38 with `--fields type,status`; `schema` 4726 → 1107 with `--fields schemas.id`.
- **The capability matrix is published** in `commands` under `agent_ops`, so a caller learns the contract instead of collecting exit codes.
- **Three fields still emitted Portuguese keys under the English default wire** — `AggregatedItem.display_url`, `AggregatedNewsItem.source`, `AggregatedNewsItem.relative_date` kept a Portuguese `serde(rename)`, and `deep-research-output.schema.json` declared the English names under `additionalProperties: false`, so a real news row FAILED the published contract.
- **Seven published envelopes carried no discriminator at all** (five `config` shapes, `locale`, `init-config`); all now emit `type` from a compiler-checked enum. All **24** published schemas are partitioned into routable and deliberately-unroutable, with the reason published as `routing`.
- **Removed `scripts/regen_cli_flags_readme.py`** — replaced by `tests/integration_docs_drift.rs`, a ruler that FAILS on divergence instead of rewriting on demand.


## What's new in v1.0.2 (2026-07)

- **ADR-0027:** serialize wire keys are **English** (`results`, `title`, `metadata`, `result_count`, `used_chrome`, `chrome_channel`, `chrome_path_resolved`, `execution_time_ms`, `news`, `searches`, `query_count`, `error`/`message`/`type`, …).
- Deserialize still accepts Portuguese aliases (fixtures/legacy).
- **`--wire-keys en|pt`** + XDG `wire_keys` — emit-boundary remap for legacy PT (`--wire-keys pt` or `config set wire_keys pt`).
- **Agent ops:** `--fields`/`--select`, `--filter`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--limit`, `--count-only`, `--truncate-content`, `--max-output-bytes`.
- **RuntimeConfig SSOT:** CLI > XDG > FACTORY (`src/runtime/`).
- **`budget_profile`:** `lab` | `desktop_contended` | `thin`.
- **`chrome_session_retries`:** CLI + XDG process-wide SERP launch retries.
- **no-warmup fail-closed:** `--no-warmup` needs hidden `--allow-no-warmup` or XDG `allow_no_warmup=true`.
- **Linux cgroup opt-in:** `linux_cgroup_enabled` + `linux_cgroup_memory_max_mb`.
- **ADR-0026 mute-audio** mandatory on every Chrome launch (MUTE-002 fixed quad-dash argv; no unmute).
- **Budget dual/contention (ADR-0025):** dual multiproc estimate, `--print-budget`, `--auto-contention-budget` (default ON), doctor `ready_for_dual_deep_research`.
- Defaults: `--max-sub-queries 3`, `--fetch-content-cap 4`; deep grace timeout **20s**.
- Fail-fast exit 2 on `budget_underflow` unless `--allow-under-budget`.
- Migration: `docs/MIGRATION.md` · `docs/MIGRATION.pt-BR.md`.


## What's new in v1.0.1 (2026-07-19) — Pass 52 agent contract

- Multi-query `--stream` / `-f ndjson` **IMPLEMENTED** — NDJSON lines of `SearchOutput` as each query completes (single-query ignores with warning).
- Dual `config` API: positional or `--key`/`--value`; `config effective` shows CLI > XDG > defaults.
- Broken pipe → exit **141**; Unix SIGPIPE stays **SIG_IGN** so oneshot reap still runs.
- Wire JSON: Portuguese serialize (1.x) + English deserialize aliases (**ADR-0023**) — **superseded serialize default by v1.0.2 EN**.
- Chrome-only CDP; no remote telemetry.


## Commands (full inventory)

```
duckduckgo-search-cli [OPTIONS] [QUERY]... [COMMAND]

Commands:
  init-config                          Write selectors.toml + user-agents.toml to XDG
  completions <SHELL>                  Shell completions (bash/zsh/fish/…)
  deep-research [OPTIONS] [QUERY]      Fan-out, aggregate, optional synthesis
  commands                             Full command tree as JSON (agent discovery)
  schema [--name NAME]                 JSON Schema catalog or named body
  doctor [--strict] [--probe-deep]
  locale                               Resolved UI locale JSON
  man [--file PATH]                    roff man page from clap tree
  config path                          Resolved config file + directory
  config list                          Allowed XDG keys
  config get <KEY>                     Read one key
  config set <KEY> <VALUE>             Write one key
  config unset <KEY>                   Remove one key
  config effective                     CLI > XDG > defaults, with source
  help
  (hidden) buscar                      Equivalent to default search mode

Root-only: --probe. Root + doctor: --probe-deep.
Global (accepted on every surface): --pre-flight, --print-schema, and the eight agent-native flags.
```

### Capability matrix — ask the binary, do not memorize a table

`duckduckgo-search-cli commands -q -f json` publishes `agent_ops[]`, one entry per surface:
`surface`, `rows` (the DECLARED row array, or absent when the surface is **rowless**),
`discriminator_key` (`type` on every surface EXCEPT `deep-research`, which routes on `kind` —
read the field, never assume it), `identity` (strings exempt from `--truncate-content`)
and `supports` (the operators that surface accepts). Read it instead of guessing — a surface
that does not support an operator REFUSES it with exit `2` and a `{"error", "message"}` envelope.

- Row surfaces (`buscar`, `deep-research`, `doctor`, `schema`, `locale`, `config list`, `config effective`, `init-config`) accept the five row operators.
- Rowless surfaces (`commands`, `config path/get/set/unset`, `--probe`, `--probe-deep`) refuse `--filter`, `--sort`, `--dedupe-by`, `--limit`, `--count-only`.
- Identity-only surfaces (`config list/path/get/set/unset/effective`, `locale`) additionally refuse `--truncate-content`.
- `--fields` and `--max-output-bytes` are accepted everywhere.

### One-liner examples

```bash
# Default search (EN wire)
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json "rust async" | jaq '.results[].url'

# Agent ops (no jaq required)
duckduckgo-search-cli "rust async" -q -f json \
  --fields url,title --filter 'title~async' --sort title --limit 5
duckduckgo-search-cli "rust async" -q -f json --count-only
duckduckgo-search-cli "rust async" -q -f json --wire-keys pt

# deep-research + budget dry-run
duckduckgo-search-cli deep-research --print-budget -q
duckduckgo-search-cli deep-research "tokio vs async-std 2026" -q -f json \
  | jaq '.results[] | {title, url, score}'

# Discovery / diagnostics
duckduckgo-search-cli init-config --force
duckduckgo-search-cli completions bash
duckduckgo-search-cli commands -q
duckduckgo-search-cli schema --name search-output
duckduckgo-search-cli --print-schema
duckduckgo-search-cli doctor -q
duckduckgo-search-cli doctor --strict
duckduckgo-search-cli doctor --probe-deep -q
duckduckgo-search-cli --probe -q
duckduckgo-search-cli locale -q
duckduckgo-search-cli man | man -l -

# config CRUD (RuntimeConfig SSOT)
duckduckgo-search-cli config path
duckduckgo-search-cli config list
duckduckgo-search-cli config get wire_keys
duckduckgo-search-cli config set budget_profile desktop_contended
duckduckgo-search-cli config set chrome_session_retries 2
duckduckgo-search-cli config set wire_keys en
duckduckgo-search-cli config unset proxy_url
duckduckgo-search-cli config effective
```


## Wire JSON (v1.0.2 default EN)

Top-level (single search): `query`, `engine`, `endpoint`, `region`, `result_count`, `results[]`, `news[]`, `news_count`, `metadata`, `pages_fetched`.

Result row: `position`, `title`, `url`, `display_url`, `snippet`, optional `content` / `content_size`.

Metadata (agent, **not** telemetry): `used_chrome`, `chrome_channel` (`host`|`flatpak`|`snap`|`manual`), `chrome_path_resolved`, `execution_time_ms`, `result_count`, `identity_used`, `zero_cause`, `next_action_suggestion`, …

Multi-query: `searches[]` / `query_count` (not `buscas`/`quantidade_queries` on default EN).

Deep top level: `kind`, `query`, `results`, `news`, `news_count`, `metadata`, `synthesis` (with `--synthesize`).
`partial` and `sub_queries_total`/`ok`/`error` live under `.metadata`, not at the top. There is no
top-level `sources`: the sources array is nested inside `synthesis`.

Thin errors: `error`, `message`, `type`.

Legacy PT: `--wire-keys pt` or `config set wire_keys pt`.

| 1.x PT | 1.0.2 EN |
|--------|--------|
| `resultados` | `results` |
| `titulo` | `title` |
| `metadados` | `metadata` |
| `quantidade_resultados` | `result_count` |
| `usou_chrome` | `used_chrome` |
| `chrome_canal` | `chrome_channel` |
| `chrome_path_resolvido` | `chrome_path_resolved` |
| `tempo_execucao_ms` | `execution_time_ms` |
| `noticias` | `news` |
| `buscas` | `searches` |
| `sintese` | `synthesis` |


## Canonical jaq (EN wire)

```bash
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json "query" | jaq '.results | length'
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json "query" | jaq -r '.results[].url'
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json "query" | jaq -r '.metadata.used_chrome // false'
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json "query" | jaq -r '.metadata.chrome_channel // "n/a"'
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json "one" "two" | jaq '.searches[0].results | length'
duckduckgo-search-cli -q -f json deep-research "query" | jaq '.results[] | {title, url, score}'
```


## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Agent action |
|------|---------|--------------|
| `0` | Success | Parse `.results` |
| `1` | Runtime error | Read stderr; retry once with `-v` |
| `2` | Config / no Chrome / budget_underflow / **agent-ops refusal** | Install Chrome; fix flags; `--print-budget` / `--allow-under-budget`; read `{"error","message"}` on stdout and the `supports` list in `commands` |
| `3` | Anti-bot block | Back off 300+ s; Chrome / `--chrome-path` / `--proxy` |
| `4` | Global timeout | Raise `--global-timeout`; reduce `--parallel` |
| `5` | Zero results | Refine query or change `--lang` |
| `6` | Suspected block | Inspect `.metadata.zero_cause`; wait 300s |
| `130` | Cancelled by SIGINT | Ctrl+C; cooperative cancel, not a failure |
| `141` | Broken pipe | Consumer closed (`\| head`); not a search failure |
| `143` | Cancelled by SIGTERM | What `timeout` sends first; not a search failure |


## Anti-patterns

- NEVER parse `text` or `markdown` with machines (use `json` + agent ops or `jaq`)
- NEVER omit outer `timeout` (pipelines hang indefinitely)
- NEVER use `.resultados` / `.metadados` on **v1.0.2** default wire (use `.results` / `.metadata` or `--wire-keys pt`)
- NEVER treat `--stream` as a full SERP hit stream (multi-query NDJSON only)
- NEVER raise `--parallel` above 5 casually (anti-bot risk)
- NEVER pass long-lived proxy secrets in argv if avoidable (prefer XDG `proxy_url`; userinfo stripped from Chrome argv in 1.0.2)
- NEVER assume an operator was applied because the exit was `0` — since **v1.0.5** every surface acts or refuses; read `agent_ops[].supports` in `commands` first
- NEVER read `agent_ops[].discriminator` — the field is `discriminator_key` since **v1.0.5**, and its value is always the key `type`
- NEVER expect `--truncate-content` to shorten an id, a config key, a locale tag or a path — those are IDENTITY and are exempt (or the surface refuses outright)


## Key flags (root)

`--num`/`-n`, `--format`/`-f`, `--output`/`-o`, `--lang`/`-l`, `--country`/`-c`, `--parallel`/`-p`,
`--vertical` (default **`all`**), `--fetch-content` / `--no-fetch-content`, `--fetch-content-cap` (default **4**),
`--stream` / `-f ndjson`, `--global-timeout` (default **180**), `--proxy` / `--no-proxy`, `--chrome-path`,
`--probe`, `--probe-deep`, `--pre-flight`, `--wire-keys`, `--fields`/`--select`, `--filter`, `--sort`,
`--dedupe-by`, `--limit`, `--count-only`, `--truncate-content`, `--max-output-bytes`, `--chrome-session-retries`,
`--no-warmup` (fail-closed without allow), `-q`, `-v`/`-vv`.

Deep-research extras: `--print-budget`, `--budget-tokens`, `--max-sub-queries` (default **3**), `--aggregate`,
`--synthesize`, `--synth-format`, `--depth`, `--allow-under-budget`, `--auto-contention-budget` /
`--no-auto-contention-budget`, `--require-all-sub-queries`, `--no-news`, `--sub-queries-file`.
